Reviewer: m3 pool job review-4261-codex-0509, GPT-6 (Codex), mkinney; did not write or refresh this PR.

Needs changes before merge: two import defects and conflicts with current main.

I read the whole diff, including the changes from #4233. I reviewed the assembly geometry path at the safety tier. The local trial merge uses upstream main `9b141e1122fad4aca12e6502dd5f4963209b4e68`. Its first parent is the PR head. I used the laws from that upstream main.

## Requested before merge

1. **Compare all component data before you reuse a row.** `crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/components.rs:22` compares only `component` and `geometry`. It omits `milling` and `running`. I exported a shared insert with 9,000 rpm and 2,400 mm/min. The destination held the same component id, code and geometry, with 4,500 rpm and 1,200 mm/min. The import succeeded and reported the row as reused. The imported tool kept 9,000 rpm, but its unchanged stack derived 4,500 rpm from the retained row. The export also lost the file's row data. This can change cutting data on a later component edit. Class: incomplete comparison of semantic data. Compare the milling facts and running data too. A different row must refuse the whole import before any write. Add tests for differences in each field.

2. **Check referenced rows before you skip an identical tool.** `crates/app/src/commands/tool_import/mod.rs:227` checks the stack links but omits the rows they reference. A skipped tool never adds its assembly to `landing`, so `components::plan` never checks its rows. I changed the `fly-25` seat position from 12.5 mm to 14.0 mm in the library. I kept the tool definition and stack links unchanged and added one plain tool. The import succeeded, skipped both assembled tools and added the plain tool. It silently kept the old 12.5 mm row. The documented id-conflict rule requires a refusal. Class: a validation bypass in the skip path. Check every referenced row before the identical-tool decision. Apply one comparison rule to all import paths. Add a test that mixes a skipped assembly with an added tool.

The probes used the PR's `assembly_cmds::shop` fixture and the public import API. Their source and executable stayed in `/tmp`. No PR source file changed.

## Local build and tests

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 356 steps; 355 passed, one failed, zero stalled.
- All mapped app suites passed. The app unit tests passed: 319 tests. `tool_library_holders` passed: 38 tests.
- `example_catalog` passed: 44 tests, four ignored. The other mapped catalog suites passed.
- Only `ui suites: shell` failed. It passed 20 tests and failed `headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero` at `crates/ui/tests/shell.rs:12`. The return code was 1; the test expected 0.
- I ran the whole shell suite on bare upstream main `9b141e1122fad4aca12e6502dd5f4963209b4e68`. It had the same 20 passes and the same assertion failure. This is a pre-existing failure and does not block this PR. I found no current tracking issue. The related historical issue #615 is closed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: six steps passed; zero failed and zero stalled. All 11 light tests passed.

## Extra suites run

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_library_holders refuses_the_file_by_name`: three tests passed. This reran both new corrupt-file tests and the existing malformed-body test.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test shell -- --nocapture` on bare main: 20 passed, one failed as stated above.

## Input mutations

- A link to `no-such` and an insert code of `CCMT09`: the readers refused the files by name. Green. The named rerun also checked bad geometry, unknown keys, duplicate rows and unused rows.
- Different running data under the same component id: accepted when refusal was required. Red; finding 1.
- A changed seat position behind identical stack links: discarded when refusal was required. Red; finding 2.

## Merge state

Main advanced during the local checks. The PR head did not change. `git merge-tree --write-tree` now finds conflicts against main `a7afb5766b5d37073eb075ecda84c3ba70430653` in:

- `crates/app/src/commands/tool_assembly.rs`
- `crates/app/src/schema.rs`
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders.rs`

The build results above apply to the stated trial merge with `9b141e1122fad4aca12e6502dd5f4963209b4e68`. I did not resolve the new conflicts. The upstream laws and ownership guard did not change between these bases. The PR needs the `needs-rework` and `conflicts` labels. Its author keeps control of its ready flag.

## Goldens and scope

No `.nc`, `.cl` or catalog golden changed. The changed example has only the project version step, 83 to 84. Its `continuous_4axis_part` suite passed. No importer or STEP fixture changed. No `crates/ui` file changed, so this PR needs no UI screenshots. Full heavy lanes did not run, as upstream law requires. The review worktree and branch remain in place for the next round.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

I merged the new #4233 head (`949b4662b`, which has main `fc8d8fbd2` with #4278) into this branch, and I fixed the two review findings of comment 7211141172. No rebase, no force-push.

**Merge commit:** `5becee8b0` (Merge issue/3645-component-library into issue/3645-camtools-v8 (#4278 lathe body)).

**Conflicted file and resolution (keep both sides):**
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders.rs`: both doc lines (`camtools_v8`, `lathe_stack`) and both modules.

**NEW CODE (commit `f21610280`):**
1. Review finding 1 (`tool_import/components.rs`): the id rule now compares the whole row except the library link: name, item, geometry, `milling`, `running` and `lathe_body`. This is the same comparison as the link-only edit of #4233. A same-id row that differs refuses the whole import by the id, before any write.
2. Review finding 2 (`tool_import/mod.rs`): when the import skips a tool as identical, each row that its stack names goes through the same rule (`components::check_skipped`). A changed row now refuses the whole import, also when other tools of the file are added. All import paths use one comparison.
3. `.camtools` v8 rows carry `lathe_body` through `component_wire` (no code change was necessary, the wire form comes from #4233).
4. Decision file `docs/decisions/3645-camtools-v8.md`: the id rule text and a "Review fix" entry.

**Pinning tests** (`crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/camtools_v8.rs`):
- `a_same_id_row_with_other_facts_running_data_or_lathe_body_refuses_the_import`: one difference for each field (`milling`, `running`, `lathe_body`). Each refuses by the id, and nothing changes.
- `a_skipped_identical_tool_whose_row_changed_refuses_the_import`: the file has a skipped assembled tool whose row `fly-25` moved its seat (12.5 -> 14.0), and an added plain tool. The import is refused, and nothing lands.
- `a_turning_stack_with_a_lathe_body_exports_and_imports_identically`: a v8 round trip of a CNMG in PCLNR stack keeps the lathe body. Export -> import -> export is byte-stable.
- I put the old comparison back for one run: the first two tests then fail. With the fix, they pass.

**Class:** DELTA (one hand-resolved test-list conflict) + NEW CODE (the review fixes and the tests).

**Gate on f21610280 (Mac):**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base 949b4662b`: 200 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (the `camcraft-app` suites of the gate map and `ui suites: catalog_render`). A first run in a target copied from the #4233 worktree gave E0463 in `catalog_render` (the known clippy/sccache target problem). The second run in an empty target is the result above.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `tool_library_holders`: 46 passed.

Ready for a re-check.
